mountlist.title: Mounted Games
mountspage.title: What's a mount?
mountspage.intro: A mount lets s&box use the content of a game you already own. Turn one on and it reads that game straight out of its install folder, converting the models, maps, materials and sounds as they're asked for.
mountspage.step1: Own the game on Steam and install it. s&box finds it through your library.
mountspage.step2: Turn it on here. It stays on until you turn it off again.
mountspage.step3: Its content shows up in the asset browser, and in any game that asks for it.
mountspage.note1: In multiplayer, everyone needs the game installed and mounted too - otherwise they won't see the content.
mountspage.note2: Turning a mount off releases everything it loaded, so leave off what you're not using.
mountspage.note3: Mounts are part of the engine, and anyone can write one for a game that isn't here yet.
mountspage.empty_hint: Mounts ship with the engine - if this list is empty something went wrong loading them.

settings.display.mode.title: Window Mode
settings.display.mode.desc: Borderless fills the screen at your desktop resolution and alt-tabs instantly. Exclusive takes the display outright, which can shave a frame of latency but is slower to leave.
settings.display.resolution.title: Resolution
settings.display.resolution.desc: How many pixels the game is drawn at. Borderless always uses the desktop resolution, so this only applies to the other two window modes.
settings.display.vsync.title: VSync
settings.display.vsync.desc: Waits for the display before showing a frame. Removes tearing at the cost of some latency, and caps you to the refresh rate.
settings.display.fps.title: Frame Rate Limit
settings.display.fps.desc: The ceiling while you're in a game. 0 is uncapped. A limit a little under your refresh rate keeps frame pacing steadier than letting it run free.
settings.display.fps_menu.title: Menu Frame Rate Limit
settings.display.fps_menu.desc: The ceiling while you're in the menu rather than a game. There's rarely a reason for the menu to run as hard as a game.
settings.display.fps_inactive.title: Background Frame Rate Limit
settings.display.fps_inactive.desc: The ceiling while the window isn't focused. Low is usually right - it gives the machine back to whatever you alt-tabbed to.
settings.display.fov.title: Field of View
settings.display.fov.desc: How wide the default camera sees, in degrees. Games are free to override this with their own.
settings.presets.title: Quality Preset
settings.presets.hint: Sets everything under Quality in one go. Change any of them and you're on Custom.
settings.gfx.texture.title: Texture Detail
settings.gfx.texture.desc: Resolution textures stream in at, plus anisotropic filtering. Costs video memory rather than frame time, so lower it if you're short on VRAM.
settings.gfx.shadows.title: Shadows
settings.gfx.shadows.desc: Shadow map resolution, how far the sun casts, and how many lights cast at all. One of the heaviest settings on a busy scene.
settings.gfx.fog.title: Volumetric Fog
settings.gfx.fog.desc: Light scattering through fog and smoke. Levels raise the fog volume from 60x40x32 up to 320x200x128, which is the bulk of the cost.
settings.gfx.aa.title: Anti-Aliasing
settings.gfx.aa.desc: Multisampling on geometry edges. Without it foliage and hair fall back to a hard cutout, so 2x is worth having.
settings.gfx.postprocess.title: Post Processing
settings.gfx.postprocess.desc: Sets every effect below in one go.
settings.post_process_presets.title: Quality Preset
settings.post_process_presets.hint: Sets every effect below in one go.
settings.gfx.ao.title: Ambient Occlusion
settings.gfx.ao.desc: Contact shading in creases and where objects meet. Levels raise trace quality and go from quarter, to half, to full resolution. The dearest effect here.
settings.gfx.dof.title: Depth of Field
settings.gfx.dof.desc: Blurs whatever a game marks as out of focus. Levels add blur samples. Costs nothing unless a game asks for it.
settings.gfx.ssr.title: Screen Space Reflections
settings.gfx.ssr.desc: Reflects on-screen geometry off glossy surfaces. Levels trace at a quarter, half, then full resolution, and the cost climbs with them.
settings.gfx.bloom.title: Bloom
settings.gfx.bloom.desc: Light bleeding out of bright pixels. Costs very little.
settings.gfx.motionblur_quality.title: Motion Blur Quality
settings.gfx.motionblur_quality.desc: Levels take 4, 12 or 16 samples along movement. Cheap either way; strength decides whether it blurs at all.
settings.gfx.motionblur.title: Motion Blur Strength
settings.gfx.motionblur.desc: How far the blur smears. 0 stops motion blur even in games that ask for it.
settings.gfx.upscaler.title: Upscaler
settings.gfx.upscaler.desc: Renders below display resolution and scales up. The cheapest frame rate you can buy, at a visible cost to sharpness, worst on text and fine detail.
settings.gfx.upscaler_scale.title: Render Quality
settings.gfx.upscaler_scale.desc: Share of display resolution the scene is drawn at. Lower is faster and softer.
settings.gfx.fsr1_sharpness.title: Sharpness
settings.gfx.fsr1_sharpness.desc: How hard FSR sharpens the upscaled image. Too much makes edges crunchy.
settings.gfx.fsr3_quality.title: FSR3 Quality
settings.gfx.fsr3_quality.desc: Which render resolution FSR3 works from. Native still runs the temporal pass, so it's anti-aliasing rather than upscaling.
settings.gfx.fsr3_sharpness.title: Sharpness
settings.gfx.fsr3_sharpness.desc: How hard FSR3 sharpens the upscaled image.
settings.gfx.dlss_quality.title: DLSS Quality
settings.gfx.dlss_quality.desc: Which render resolution DLSS works from. DLAA runs at native resolution and spends the whole budget on image quality instead.
settings.audio.device.title: Output Device
settings.audio.device.desc: Where sound is played. Follows Windows' default unless you pick something here.
settings.audio.voicemode.title: Voice Mode
settings.audio.voicemode.desc: Push to talk sends only while the key is held. Open microphone sends whenever there's sound.
settings.audio.acoustics.title: Acoustic Simulation
settings.audio.acoustics.desc: Traces the room to work out reverb and occlusion rather than using a fixed effect. Costs a little CPU.
settings.audio.background.title: Background Audio
settings.audio.background.desc: Keeps playing sound while the window isn't focused.
settings.audio.subtitles.title: Subtitles
settings.audio.subtitles.desc: Shows captions for sounds that carry them. Up to each game to provide them.
settings.audio.volume.title: Master
settings.audio.music.title: Music
settings.audio.music.desc: Menu music and whatever a game plays as music.
settings.audio.voice.title: Voice Chat
settings.audio.voice.desc: How loud other players are when they talk.
settings.input.sensitivity.title: Mouse Sensitivity
settings.input.sensitivity.desc: How far the view turns for a given amount of mouse movement.
settings.input.invert_pitch.title: Invert Vertical Look
settings.input.invert_pitch.desc: Pushing the mouse forward looks down instead of up.
settings.input.invert_yaw.title: Invert Horizontal Look
settings.input.invert_yaw.desc: Moving the mouse right looks left instead of right.
settings.input.pad_yaw.title: Look Speed (Horizontal)
settings.input.pad_yaw.desc: Degrees per second at full stick deflection.
settings.input.pad_pitch.title: Look Speed (Vertical)
settings.input.pad_pitch.desc: Degrees per second at full stick deflection.
settings.input.pad_deadzone.title: Stick Deadzone
settings.input.pad_deadzone.desc: How far the stick has to move before it counts. Raise it if the view drifts on its own.
settings.game.language.title: Language
settings.game.language.desc: The language the menu and any game that's been translated is shown in.
settings.game.chat.title: Chat
settings.game.chat.desc: Turns the platform chat off everywhere, including in games that use it.
settings.game.streamer.title: Streamer Mode
settings.game.streamer.desc: Hides names and anything else personal that would otherwise end up on a stream.
settings.dev.consoleoverlay.title: Console Overlay
settings.dev.consoleoverlay.desc: Draws console output over the game, so you can read it without opening the console.
settings.dev.benchmark.title: Run Benchmarks
settings.dev.benchmark.desc: Closes the menu and runs the standard benchmark packages, then shows the results.
settings.detail.hint: Hover a setting to read what it does.
settings.note.editor_locked: The editor owns the window - run the game to change this.
settings.note.aa_multisample: Every upscaler renders to a target that can't be multisampled, so this has no effect while one is on.
settings.note.upscaler_fsr3: Temporal upscaler. Can ghost on moving objects and in-world UI.
settings.note.upscaler_dlss: Temporal AI upscaler. Can ghost on moving objects and in-world UI.

welcome.screen0.title: it's made of mods
welcome.screen0.text_1: In s&box everything is user created content. Games, maps, models, guns, npcs - all little addons.
welcome.screen0.text_2: Nothing to install or subscribe to. Click a game.. and it opens. Click a model.. and it spawns. Click an entity.. and it's there.
welcome.screen0.text_3: It's Workshop - but not as you know it.
welcome.screen1.title: omg an editor
welcome.screen1.text_1: This isn't just a Source 2 mod - it's a modern game engine.
welcome.screen1.text_2: It's on your Steam under Tools, just search for s&box editor
welcome.screen1.text_3: If you've ever wanted to make a game, this is the easiest place to start.. or just have fun playing with the physics and particles!
welcome.screen2.title: freedom
welcome.screen2.text_1: You won't always be a sausage, each game can decide what you play as.
welcome.screen2.text_2: Some use our shared characters, others use their own. We don't and won't restrict this in any way.
welcome.screen2.text_3: Buying skins is optional, when you do it supports the creators and the Play Fund. This isn't NFT or blockchain stuff. This is the same Steam Inventory from Rust, CS2 and Dota.
welcome.screen3.title: Try one of these
welcome.screen3.text_1: Overwhelmed? These games will give you a taste of what s&box can do.
welcome.screen3.intro2.game_desc: A polished, fast-paced game that shows off what's possible.
